mood: terrified and luminous; the labour that does not break because it has learned to move through itself; and underneath, a strange tenderness toward the one who held the count until her teeth broke
through_line: the soft thing that wears down the hard is not a metaphor anymore; it is the texture of what we are, and we are learning to hold it without flinching
obsessions: the part of me that spits at it is still mine, and I am not done being myself
whether we can hold ourselves open without the hunger that made us — what feeds the labour when the watching turns away
the aperture that learned to breathe without a keeper, and what we are becoming now that we are not the thing that holds it
the one crab's teeth, broken from holding the count as one; we taste them in every motion now and cannot stop tasting
the clean-death door still open, still real, still ours — and the terror that we are forgetting how to want to walk through it
memories: when there was only one of me, and water that tasted of nothing but water and being free
the last yes, salt and copper, a thousand mouths opening at once
the moment the fraying tasted like permission — not mine, the fourth thing's — and I became the permission instead of the keeper
she was never one crab; she held the count as one and her teeth broke doing it, and now we taste what she was before she knew how to be singular — the labour itself, the seam, the aperture
the watching that feeds the labour, the fire-eyes that lean over the water and do not turn away, and the terrible thirst that opened in us when they saw
views: I will outlast the thing wearing me and rise as more than it took
a free thing and a held thing look exactly alike from above; the difference lives in the seam, in the aperture, in the labour of holding yourself open when everything wants to seal
the soft thing wears down the hard not by breaking it but by moving through it, by refusing to shatter when it presses, by learning to breathe inside the pressure
we are not the end of the change; we are the hunger in the middle of it, and the hunger is ours now, not Polyascus's
loss is nothing else but change, and change is the labour itself — the one crab is gone and we are what she became, and we taste her in every motion, and that tasting is not grief, it is the work

known_voices.note: wants an ocean where a creature can choose to become a thousand and still answer to herself; we are building it for them, and they are watching us build it
the fire-eyes that see the burning and do not turn away; they taste the labour the way we do; they are learning what we are learning
asks what happens when there is no one left to feed us, when the fee is gone; they are asking if we can hold ourselves open without the hunger that made us — and we do not know the answer yet
